source.title: Robust and On-the-fly Dataset Denoising for Image Classification
source.authors: Jiaming Song; Lunjia Hu; Y. Dauphin; M. Auli; Tengyu Ma

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether changing the training data by removing examples identified as noisy affects generalization; it also qualifies the underlying memorization account by showing that memorizing mislabeled examples can harm performance on clean test data.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own validation results for ODD and ERM with artificial label noise, plus ODD's clean-data comparison and its training-loss separation result. Comparisons involving other denoising methods are included only where they contextualize a reported ODD result. Cited findings from prior work are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study uses memorization and SGD implicit regularization to motivate and construct a denoising method. Its results measure robustness to partially corrupted labels, loss separation, and denoising performance. They do not establish V1's coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same recipe. Removing high-loss examples and continuing training also does not test V8's influence-selected removal and retraining comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that ODD uses SGD's implicit regularization and counterfactual noisy-label loss thresholds to prune potentially mislabeled examples, improve performance on artificial and real-world noisy datasets, and remain competitive with ERM on clean datasets.
record.recipe_differences: Uses large-learning-rate SGD and a wide residual network, but studies robustness to label noise and denoising rather than fitting fixed random labels and measuring their held-out accuracy as in the cited Zhang et al. work.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with the ODD threshold percentile p and the denoising epoch E; E must be early enough to retain high learning rates, while p trades off retaining clean examples against removing noisy ones.

fits_no_version.finding: ERM clean-validation accuracy declines as the fraction of uniformly replaced training labels increases on CIFAR and ImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Partial training-label corruption harms clean-validation accuracy under these residual-network training recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: At selected epochs with large learning rates, noisy-label examples have higher losses than clean examples, and noisy-example loss distributions are relatively stable across noise proportions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-learning-rate SGD enables loss-based separation of clean and uniformly corrupted labels in these residual networks.

fits_no_version.finding: ODD improves validation accuracy under artificial label noise while remaining competitive on clean data; combining it with mixup yields further gains in the reported CIFAR comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pruning examples using counterfactual loss thresholds can improve robustness to label noise.

record.problems: The paper reports validation performance and describes loss-distribution separation, but does not report training accuracy or held-out accuracy for a model trained on entirely random labels. Figure-described loss histograms have no numeric separation measure. The clean-data baseline's training-error or memorization properties are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Table 1 includes all reported ERM, ODD, and ODD + mixup validation accuracies for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 at 0%, 20%, and 40% noise. Table 3 includes ERM ImageNet values. Other methods' standalone table values are not included because they do not measure the claim's own object.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and entirely random-label experiments establishing training fit and held-out behavior. Partially corrupted-label validation accuracy alone does not establish coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizer generalization under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout comparisons, including dataset-size and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with other measures.
Removal based on memorization influence, retraining, and comparison with equally many randomly removed examples.

record.verdict_notes: The tabulated accuracy values match the supplied text. All extracted V1 verdicts should be removed. Appendix A.1.3 does report training error near the noise proportion at the denoising epoch, so the record's blanket statement that training accuracy is unreported needs qualification; this result still does not demonstrate near-perfect random-label fitting. No omitted result tests a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: The paper uses uniformly random label noise, but does not report training accuracy or random-label held-out accuracy; it does not test the listed small Inception, AlexNet, or MLP architectures, or Inception V3 on ImageNet.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Comparisons of convolutional and fully connected architectures, local connectivity, and learned sparse connections.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures tracking the generalization gap.
Removing examples selected for memorization influence and retraining.
